title: PortFast and BPDU Guard: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: You plug in a computer. And the port makes you wait thirty seconds before it works. That's spanning tree being careful. Let's speed it up, safely.

scenes.heading: The hotel key card
scenes.narration: Walk into a hotel and swipe your card. The door opens at once. That's PortFast. Now picture a hotel that first checks with the front desk whether anyone else is already in the room. That's slow, but safe. Normal spanning tree is the cautious hotel. PortFast skips the wait for ports that only ever lead to a guest's room, meaning an end device. But what if someone plugs in a switch there? That's where B P D U Guard steps in and shuts the door.

items.story: The door shuts if a switch appears

scenes.heading: The commands
scenes.narration: Turn on PortFast for the port. Then turn on B P D U Guard. If a B P D U ever arrives, the port goes into error disabled.

lines.note: Skip the wait on this port
Shut the port if a BPDU arrives

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three mix-ups. PortFast isn't a replacement for spanning tree. It only skips the waiting. Don't put it on trunk ports, because that can cause loops. And B P D U Guard doesn't turn spanning tree off. It shuts the port down when something unexpected shows up.

items.right: STP still runs; only the wait is skipped
Only on access ports, never trunks

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva PortFast and BPDU Guard lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. PortFast makes access ports start forwarding immediately. B P D U Guard shuts a port if a switch is plugged in. Use them together on every user port. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva PortFast and BPDU Guard lab.

points.t: PortFast: instant start on access ports
BPDU Guard: err-disables on a BPDU
Use both on every user port
